summary: Both editions were independently reviewed against every clause of the selected Greek working source. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the complete negations, repentance conditions, emptiness metaphor, great-demon assertion, and consequence involving the women who work evil against them. The simplified edition retains these meanings despite sentence splitting. The notes distinguish the printed conjecture “foolish” from the reported partial wickedness reading and accurately reflect the supplied bounded project report without claiming manuscript unanimity. Acceptance concerns fidelity to this working source and the supplied disclosures; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts, certify an exhaustive collation, or establish a unique interpretation.
